summary: Interpreted the end-to-end stale-read probe, which closes the last limitation this question carried. Each trial committed a value before the partition, had the successor at term 3 commit a different value, and then read the mock FSM on both nodes after the verify returned: all five trials show the divergence the consequence needs — the stalled leader still held 'old' while the successor held 'new' — and in the two trials where the verify returned success (parsed indices 1 and 7, reconnections 300ms and 450ms) a caller following the documented pattern would have read 'old' from a node it had just been told was still the leader while the cluster's state was 'new'. The other three trials answered leadership loss, so the stale read only matters when the verify succeeds and the per-trial choice recorded earlier stands. The account now cites that receipt, replaces the limitation saying the FSM read was never exercised, and lists the Fact it relies on; the Fact was extended under its own id with the third execution, the FSM values, and the per-execution success counts kept separate rather than averaged. No execution requested.
